title: Real-rootedness of the type B Eulerian transformation — Chris Ozols
shortTitle: Real-rootedness of the type B Eulerian transformation
description: Lean-checked proof of the Eulerian-map claim in Athanasiadis’s Remark 7.2(b), for every degree. No novelty or priority claimed.
summary: The type B Eulerian transformation sends every nonzero polynomial in Athanasiadis’s cone to a polynomial whose roots are all real and negative.

problem.name: Athanasiadis’s type B Eulerian transformation conjecture
problem.sourceHtml: Remark 7.2(b) of On the real-rootedness of the Eulerian transformation.

verification.summary: Lean 4.35.0 with Mathlib and RealRooted; the repository includes the axiom audit and build results.

priority.statement: No novelty or priority is claimed. Related work by Liu and Yan may imply the same result; that overlap is unresolved.

statementHtml: Let ℬ be the linear map taking tm to the type B Eulerian polynomial Bm(x). For every n ≥ 0 and every nonzero nonnegative linear combination of tn−k(1+t)k for 0 ≤ k ≤ n, its image under ℬ has degree n and all roots are real and strictly negative, counted with multiplicity.
scopeHtml: This proves the Eulerian-map part of Remark 7.2(b). The companion derangement claim and the stronger conclusions about simple roots and strict interlacing are not part of this Lean result.
proofOutlineHtml: The ordinary Eulerian polynomial provides a common interlacer for the basis images. The needed signs are preserved under nonnegative linear combinations. See the proof.
verificationHtml: The Lean restatement uses Mathlib’s standard polynomial definitions. The verification report records a clean build and checks that the audited declarations use only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
priorArtHtml: The prior-art review documents the possible overlap with Liu and Yan and the limits of the search.
provenanceHtml: Chris Ozols directed the work, with AI-assisted proof development and formalization on top of RealRooted. See the provenance notes.
